newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tanker rates up on new Iraq fixture.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tanker rates up on new Iraq fixture.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering rates for eastwards voyages from the Middle East firmed on Wednesday on the first Iraq-Japan fixture since the implementation of the U.N. oil for food deal, brokers said.

They said Petrodiamond on behalf of Mitsubishi had fixed a 250,000 tonne Very Large Crude carrier (VLCC) from Mina al-Bakr to Japan at W66, to load on January 24. This compares with W62.5 for earlier Mideast/Japan fixtures.
"Japan has a preference for modern vessels and the loading is five weeks away. It's a small price to pay," one broker said.

He said the fact that the Mitsubishi deal still has to receive the go-ahead from the United Nations also meant it was subject a small premium, although he believed the go-ahead was little more than a formality.
"All the AG (Mideast Gulf) is slightly firming. It's a matter of mood, with Iraq as a new supply source."
Brokers described the inter-U.K./Cont market as bullish but nervous for 80,000 tonners.
"There are more cargoes than ships but the market is very nervous," one said. He put the rate for 80,000 tonners at W110 or more, "but nobody is really sure."
But for 130,000 tonners he described the mood as bearish with few fixtures seen, as was the case for North Sea to USAC with W80 talked against W82.5 or higher on Tuesday.

The Mediterranean was likewise quiet. "There are few cargoes around with nothing being fixed," said a Med broker, putting the rate for Aframaxes (80,000 tonners) at W105-110, little changed from two fixings seen earlier at W110 for cross-Med hops.

West Africa was steady at around W62.5 for 260,000 tonners to the U.S. Gulf and W82.5 for 130,000 tonners, brokers said, while Caribs/USG-USAC were worth W155 for 70,000 tonners, up slightly from W152.5.
